title_content.content: Bromotrifluoromethoxylation of allenes: expedient access to allylic trifluoromethoxy derivatives†

paragraph_content.content: Cite this: Org Chem Front , 2025, 12, 3960
Received 27th December 2024, Accepted 21st March 2025
Rui Liu,<sup>a</sup> Yangdong Hou *<sup>b</sup> and Pingping Tang*<sup>a,b</sup>
rsc.li/frontiers-organic

A mild and eficient method for the bromotrifluoromethoxylation of allenes has been explored using trifluoromethyl arylsulfonate (TFMS) as the trifluoromethoxy source. A series of allylic trifluoromethoxy derivatives were obtained with high yields and good regioselectivity by terminal selectivity of the allenes. This transition metal-free process expands the scope of the application of trifluoromethoxy reagents.

The introduction of fluorinated functional groups into organic molecules has a significant impact on their physical and chemical properties.<sup>1</sup> Thus, more and more fluorinated drug molecules are being synthesized.<sup>2</sup> In particular, the trifluoromethoxy group (OCF ) brings good metabolic stability and high lipophilicity to molecules, earning it the nickname of superhalogen.<sup>3</sup> The unique physical and chemical properties of trifluoromethoxy functional groups have attracted attention in the fields of materials science and pharmaceuticals. However, the number of marketed drugs and agricultural chemicals containing
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }
remains low, and the study of
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }
is largely behind the development of other fluorinated functional groups. Pioneering works have focused on the construction of the
\mathrm { O - C F } _ { 3 }
bond from an already installed OH group, but this indirect method usually requires harsh conditions or toxic reagents
( e . g .
, HF and
Directly introducing an
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }

functional group is an efective alternative method for obtaining trifluoromethoxylated compounds.<sup>5</sup> However, this is limited by the reversible decomposition of trifluoromethoxy and trifluoromethoxylation reagents.

In 2017, our research group developed trifluoromethyl benzenesulfonate (TFMS) as a trifluoromethoxy reagent, which can be synthesized in one step from Togni reagent. It has been used to achieve the first asymmetric trifluoromethoxylation reaction, realizing internal trifluoromethoxylation selectivity of alkenes (Scheme 1a).<sup>6</sup> Allenes exist in many natural products and pharmaceuticals.<sup>7</sup> The high activity of allenes makes them widely used as synthons for cyclization,<sup>8</sup> hydrogenheteroatom reactions<sup>9</sup> and multifunctionalization.<sup>10</sup> With our continuous eforts on the trifluoromethoxylation reactions,<sup>11</sup> we speculated that if allenes were subjected to our reaction system,
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }

would simultaneously be easily introduced into the products. However, the reaction of allenes presented more complex reactivity than that of alkenes. The versatile reactivities of allenes allow for the selective modification of diferent positions, enabling the synthesis of diferent regioselectivity functionalized compounds,<sup>12</sup> which could deliver more possible trifluoromethoxylation products. This interesting but questionable selectivity motivated us to investigate this chemistry. Conversely, due to the toxic reagents and the cost of transition metal catalysts or metallic reagents, transition metalfree processes with readily available
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }

sources have always attracted the attention of chemists. Herein, we report our eforts to develop a transition metal-free process for bromotrifluoromethoxylation of allenes with our trifluoromethoxy reagent (Scheme 1b).

To validate our hypothesis, the initial study focused on the reaction of substrate 1a, which was treated with the previous olefin reaction conditions. We were delighted to find the bromosubstituted allyl trifluoromethoxy product 3a in 24% yield with excellent regioselectivity but poor stereoselectivity (see Table S1 in the ESI†). We did not detect the benzyl trifluoromethoxylation product, similar to the olefin reactions in our previous work. Meanwhile, 3a was obtained in 11% yield without the addition of silver fluoride and the ligand (Table 1, entry 1). NBS delivered the product in 16% yield and resulted in 56 : 44 E/Z selectivity. Other bromination reagents, such as TBCA, PHBP, TBCO and N-bromosaccharin aforded the desired product in less than 5% yield (Table 1, entries 3–6). Further optimization of the bromination reagents revealed that TBATB provided the best results, giving the corresponding product 3a in 86% yield with 84 : 16 E/Z selectivity (Table 1, entry 7). The product 3a was obtained with 76/24 E/Z selectivity when using 2 equivalents of TBATB (Table 1, entry 8). 3a cannot be obtained when using NaF or
\mathrm { C a F } _ { 2 } ,

perhaps due to the poor solubility of these two fluoride salts (Table 1, entries 9 and 11). Otherwise, KF can aford 3a in 63% yield (Table 1, entry 10). However, the yield significantly decreased to 27% using silver fluoride (Table 1, entry 12). When the reaction was performed at
4 0 \ ^ { \circ } \mathbf { C } _ { : }
, the conversion after 16 h was slightly reduced (Table 1, entry 13). Meanwhile, upon heating the reaction mixture to 60 °C, compound 3a was isolated in 78% yield (Table 1, entry 14).

paragraph_content.content: To evaluate the practicability and eficiency of this reaction, a gram-scale synthesis of 3a was conducted under the standard reaction conditions in 73% yield (Scheme 3a). Further transformation of the bromoallylic trifluoromethoxy products for the construction of a series of OCF -containing compounds was investigated (Scheme 3b). Under hydrogenation conditions, alkyl trifluoromethoxy 5a can be obtained with a yield of 61%. Propargyl trifluoromethoxy compound 5b was produced with a yield of 46% by eliminating hydrogen bromide.

To gain more insight into the reaction mechanism, we carried out some control experiments (see Schemes S2 and S3 in the ESI†). Monitoring of the reaction between 1a and TBATB by <sup>1</sup>H NMR spectrum showed that the characteristic hydrogen of the allene has undergone a shift. The HRMS-ESI (m/z) results indicated that alkene bromide ions were generated in the reaction (Scheme 4). This indicates the appearance of bromonium active intermediates. Meanwhile, we also conducted D-NOESY NMR spectra of 3a and 3d to confirm the configuration (see Schemes S4–S6 in the ESI†).<sup>13</sup>

paragraph_content.content: Organic Chemistry Frontiers
We have presented the first example of bromotrifluoromethoxylation of allenes using TFMS as an
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }
source. By the combination of TBATB with CsF, a transition metal-free process with a readily available
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }
source provided a range of allylic trifluoromethoxy derivatives in up to 86% yield and with complete regiocontrol, which are dificult to access by other methods. Due to the easy decomposition of the
\mathrm { O C F } _ { 3 }

group, carefully selecting the appropriate bromine source, reaction temperature, solvent, and base were very critical, as all the factors jointly guaranteed the smooth transformation. This discovery also expanded the scope of the application of the trifluoromethoxy reagent.
